信.meaning: A stranger hangs his hat on your <part>coat hook</part> and gives a <part>speech</part>: 'Lend me your bike, I'll bring it back by six.' No proof, no deposit. You hand it over anyway. That's <kanji>faith</kanji>.
信.on: At six on the dot he's back with your bike, limping: he banged his <sound>shin</sound> on the pedal.

刻.meaning: An <part>acrobat</part> tumbles across the room and, mid-flip, flicks a <part>dagger</part> at a block of wood. Scratch, scratch: each flip carves one more letter of her name. When she lands, it's there for good. She can <kanji>engrave</kanji> anything.
刻.on: A <sound>cock</sound>atoo lands on the block and pecks a curly tail onto the last letter.
刻.kun: Next she carves a <sound>key</sound> into the wood and sells it at the ba<sound>za</sound>ar.

走.meaning: Your feet kick up <part>soil</part> as you race down the track, one foot pushing off like a <part>skate</part> blade, long stride after long stride. Wind in your hair, heart pounding: you <kanji>run</kanji>.
走.on: Then you step on a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p and slide the rest of the way.
走.kun: You run past a <sound>hu</sound>t where a knight waves his <sound>shi</sound>eld and cheers you on.

起.meaning: A <part>runner</part> is fast asleep on the track when a <part>cobra</part> slithers over and hisses right in her ear. Her eyes snap open and she's off like a shot. Nothing will <kanji>rouse</kanji> you faster.
起.on: She had locked the cobra in a box, but it stole the <sound>key</sound>.
起.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she gasps as the cobra's tongue tickles her nose, and she leaps out of bed.

馬.meaning: A tall shape with a flowing mane gallops across a bed of <part>hot coals</part>, four hooves flicking up sparks. It snorts, it neighs, and it never once slows down. It's a brave <kanji>horse</kanji>.
馬.on: After its run, the coals are just right for a <sound>ba</sound>rbecue.
馬.kun: The horse slurps a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don and drinks tea from a giant <sound>mu</sound>g.

駅.meaning: Long ago a <part>horse</part> ran from town to town, and at every stop someone would <part>measure</part> out oats and water. Fresh horse in, tired horse out. Today the trains still stop at the same spot: the <kanji>station</kanji>.
駅.on: On the platform, a spiky <sound>ech</sound>idna waits for the next train.

返.meaning: You roll a ball up a <part>ramp</part>, but the ramp is <part>anti</part> everything: it shoves the ball straight back down to your feet. Up it goes again, and back it comes. Whatever you send, it will <kanji>return</kanji>.
返.on: A <sound>hen</sound> at the top kicks the ball back down with one claw.
返.kun: You give a <sound>ca</sound>rp back to the pond and an <sound>e</sound>gg back to the hen.
